# Independent SVG mask controls

Generated by `tools/svg_mask_fixture.py`, using original six-column artwork and
original PNG/JPEG pixels. No corpus artwork is included. The DOCX repeats it as
a full picture, cropped picture, grouped picture and shape fill.

Columns exercise user-space half masks, gray luminance, 50% white opacity,
object-bounding-box content coordinates, an embedded PNG luminance mask and an
embedded JPEG with an sRGB invert color matrix. The reference application renders all four
contexts in the retained one-page PDF.

`tools/capture-svg-group-raster.ps1` captured the first inline picture's owned
reference-application range. `tools/record_svg_masks.py` extracted its nested SVG metafile and six
original PNGs. `metafile-reference.json` records source/capture/native/image
hashes, pixel dimensions, transforms and middle-column RGBA. The original PNGs
avoid PDF's additional premultiplication of transparent RGB.

The gray mask has alpha 128 and the opacity=.5 mask has alpha 127. The reference application preview
opacity correction reproduces that difference. Browser tests check decoded
interior coverage/alpha, source immutability, cleanup, translucent groups with
masked/filtered children and the complete DOCX edit/undo/export/reopen workflow.
The full native/browser page comparison confirms all four contexts render.
Edge-pixel equivalence remains open: The reference application's intrinsic raster bounds overlap
adjacent strips, while browser masking leaves narrow seams. The retained native
bounds and images support that ongoing fidelity work; interior samples alone
must not be treated as proof of full pixel equivalence.
